source_refs.note: Book p. 179-181: 10.1.2 deductions 1-10, results (i)-(x). Book error: deduction 7 prints 'Let a = 2pi and b = phi' (working uses theta). Teaching notes, Exam tip, Key points, Common mistakes are ours.

blocks.text: Pichle page par humne ek qanoon saabit kiya tha: \(\cos(\alpha - \beta) = \cos\alpha\cos\beta + \sin\alpha\sin\beta\). Aaj hum dekhenge ke is ek qanoon se kitne saare formulas nikalte hain. Kitab das (10) deductions (natije) nikaalti hai, jin ke results (i) se (x) tak number kiye gaye hain. Har deduction mein tareeqa ek hi hai: kisi purane formula mein angle ki jagah koi samajhdaari wali value rakh do, aur naya formula haazir. Is page ko kahani ki tarah parhiye: har natija agle natije ki seerhi banta hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Shuru karne se pehle yeh values zehan mein taaza kar lijiye, poore page par yahi kaam aayengi: \(\cos\frac{\pi}{2} = 0\), \(\sin\frac{\pi}{2} = 1\), \(\cos 2\pi = 1\), \(\sin 2\pi = 0\). Aur negative angles ke liye: \(\cos(-\theta) = \cos\theta\) (cos minus sign ko nigal jata hai) aur \(\sin(-\theta) = -\sin\theta\) (sin minus sign bahar nikaal deta hai).
Deduction 1

Hum jaante hain ke:
\[\cos(\alpha - \beta) = \cos\alpha\cos\beta + \sin\alpha\sin\beta\]
Is mein \(\alpha = \frac{\pi}{2}\) rakhein, to
\[\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - \beta\right)\]
\[= \cos\frac{\pi}{2}\cos\beta + \sin\frac{\pi}{2}\sin\beta\]
\[\Rightarrow \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - \beta\right) = 0 \cdot \cos\beta + 1 \cdot \sin\beta\]
\(\left(\because \cos\frac{\pi}{2} = 0,\ \sin\frac{\pi}{2} = 1\right)\)
Lihaza

blocks.text_alt: cos of (pi over 2 minus beta) equals sin beta, result (i)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: \(\frac{\pi}{2} - \beta\) aur \(\beta\) complementary angles (aise angles jin ka jama \(90^{\circ}\) ho) hain. Result (i) kehta hai: kisi angle ka cos, us ke complement ka sin hota hai. Misaal: \(\cos 60^{\circ} = \sin 30^{\circ} = \frac{1}{2}\). Isi liye to naam bhi 'co-sine' hai: complement ka sine!
Deduction 2

Hum jaante hain ke:
\[\cos(\alpha - \beta) = \cos\alpha\cos\beta + \sin\alpha\sin\beta\]
Is mein \(\beta = -\frac{\pi}{2}\) rakhein, to
\[\cos\left[\alpha - \left(-\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\right]\]
\[= \cos\alpha\cos\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}\right) + \sin\alpha\sin\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\]
\[\Rightarrow \cos\left(\alpha + \frac{\pi}{2}\right) = \cos\alpha \cdot 0 + \sin\alpha(-1)\]
\(\left[\because \sin\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}\right) = -\sin\frac{\pi}{2} = -1\right.\),
\(\left.\cos\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}\right) = \cos\frac{\pi}{2} = 0\right]\)
Lihaza

blocks.text_alt: cos of (pi over 2 plus alpha) equals minus sin alpha, result (ii)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: \(\cos(-\theta) = \cos\theta\) aur \(\sin(-\theta) = -\sin\theta\) kyun? Angle \(-\theta\) ka matlab hai \(\theta\) ko ulti taraf (clockwise, ghari ki suiyon ki taraf) naapna. Unit circle par is ka point \((\cos\theta, \sin\theta)\) ka \(x\)-axis mein aaina-aks (mirror image) hai, yani \((\cos\theta, -\sin\theta)\). \(x\)-coordinate (cos) wahi rehta hai, \(y\)-coordinate (sin) ka sign badal jata hai. Shakal bana kar dekhiye, foran samajh aa jayega.
Deduction 3

Ab hum result (i) ko hi auzaar banate hain:
\[\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - \beta\right) = \sin\beta \quad \text{[(i) above]}\]
Is mein \(\beta = \frac{\pi}{2} + \alpha\) rakhein, to
\[\cos\left[\frac{\pi}{2} - \left(\frac{\pi}{2} + \alpha\right)\right] = \sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2} + \alpha\right)\]
\[\Rightarrow \cos(-\alpha) = \sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2} + \alpha\right)\]
\[\Rightarrow \cos\alpha = \sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2} + \alpha\right)\]
\([\because \cos(-\alpha) = \cos\alpha]\)

blocks.text_alt: sin of (pi over 2 plus alpha) equals cos alpha, result (iii)

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Result (iii) ko \(\alpha = 30^{\circ}\) par parakhiye: \(\sin 120^{\circ}\) aur \(\cos 30^{\circ}\), dono \(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) hain na? Isi tarah (ii) ko parakhiye: \(\cos 120^{\circ} = -\frac{1}{2}\) aur \(-\sin 30^{\circ} = -\frac{1}{2}\).
Deduction 4

Hum jaante hain ke:
\[\cos(\alpha - \beta) = \cos\alpha\cos\beta + \sin\alpha\sin\beta\]
Ab \(\beta\) ki jagah \(-\beta\) rakhein, to
\[\cos[\alpha - (-\beta)] = \cos\alpha\cos(-\beta) + \sin\alpha\sin(-\beta)\]
\([\because \cos(-\beta) = \cos\beta,\ \sin(-\beta) = -\sin\beta]\)

blocks.text_alt: cos of (alpha plus beta) equals cos alpha cos beta minus sin alpha sin beta, result (iv)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: (iv) ko asal law se milaiye: bracket ke andar ka sign badla to beech ka sign bhi badal gaya. \(\cos(\alpha - \beta)\) mein \(+\), \(\cos(\alpha + \beta)\) mein \(-\). Yaad rakhne ka tareeqa: cos wale formula mein sign hamesha ulta hota hai. Yahan sirf ek chhoti si tabdeeli, \(\beta\) se \(-\beta\), ne poora naya formula de diya.
Deduction 5

Hum jaante hain ke:
\[\cos(\alpha + \beta) = \cos\alpha\cos\beta - \sin\alpha\sin\beta\]
Ab \(\alpha\) ki jagah \(\frac{\pi}{2} + \alpha\) rakhein, to
\[\cos\left[\left(\frac{\pi}{2} + \alpha\right) + \beta\right]\]
\[= \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2} + \alpha\right)\cos\beta - \sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2} + \alpha\right)\sin\beta\]
\[\Rightarrow \cos\left[\frac{\pi}{2} + (\alpha + \beta)\right] = -\sin\alpha\cos\beta - \cos\alpha\sin\beta\]
\[\Rightarrow -\sin(\alpha + \beta) = -[\sin\alpha\cos\beta + \cos\alpha\sin\beta]\]
\(\therefore\)

blocks.text_alt: sin of (alpha plus beta) equals sin alpha cos beta plus cos alpha sin beta, result (v)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Teesri line kaise aayi? Yeh is page ka sab se mushkil qadam hai, is liye dhyan se: right side par humne (ii) \(\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2} + \alpha\right) = -\sin\alpha\) aur (iii) \(\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2} + \alpha\right) = \cos\alpha\) rakhe. Left side par result (ii) hi laga, bas \(\alpha\) ki jagah poora \((\alpha + \beta)\) aa gaya: \(\cos\left[\frac{\pi}{2} + (\alpha + \beta)\right] = -\sin(\alpha + \beta)\). Ab dono taraf minus hai; dono ko \(-1\) se multiply karein, minus khatam, aur sin ka sum formula (v) mil gaya. Yahi formula Example 2 mein istemal hua tha.
Deduction 6

Hum jaante hain ke:
\[\sin(\alpha + \beta) = \sin\alpha\cos\beta + \cos\alpha\sin\beta \quad \text{[from (v) above]}\]
Ab \(\beta\) ki jagah \(-\beta\) rakhein, to
\[\sin(\alpha - \beta) = \sin\alpha\cos(-\beta) + \cos\alpha\sin(-\beta)\]
\(\left\{\because \sin(-\beta) = -\sin\beta,\ \cos(-\beta) = \cos\beta\right.\)
\(\therefore\)

blocks.text_alt: sin of (alpha minus beta) equals sin alpha cos beta minus cos alpha sin beta, result (vi)

blocks.title: Dhyan dein
blocks.text: Sin wale formulas mein sign bracket ke sign jaisa hi rehta hai: sum mein plus, difference mein minus. Cos mein ulta. Bas yeh ek farq yaad kar lein to chaaron formulas kabhi nahin bhoolenge.
Deduction 7

Hum jaante hain ke:
\[\cos(\alpha - \beta) = \cos\alpha\cos\beta + \sin\alpha\sin\beta\]
Maan lijiye \(\alpha = 2\pi\) aur \(\beta = \theta\)
\[\therefore \cos(2\pi - \theta) = \cos 2\pi\cos\theta + \sin 2\pi\sin\theta\]
\[= 1 \cdot \cos\theta + 0 \cdot \sin\theta\]
\(\because \cos 2\pi = 1,\ \sin 2\pi = 0\)
\[= \cos\theta \quad \text{(vii)}\]

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab yahan \(\beta = \varphi\) chhaapti hai, jab ke aage poora hisaab \(\theta\) mein hai. Sahi yeh hai: \(\alpha = 2\pi\) aur \(\beta = \theta\). Hum ne upar sahi likha hai.
Deduction 8

Hum jaante hain ke:
\[\sin(\alpha - \beta) = \sin\alpha\cos\beta - \cos\alpha\sin\beta\]
\[\sin(2\pi - \theta) = \sin 2\pi\cos\theta - \cos 2\pi\sin\theta\]
\[= 0 \cdot \cos\theta - 1 \cdot \sin\theta\]
\(\because \sin 2\pi = 0,\ \cos 2\pi = 1\)
\[= -\sin\theta \quad \text{(viii)}\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Yahan kitab ne (vi) mein \(\alpha = 2\pi\) aur \(\beta = \theta\) rakh diya hai, magar likha nahin; aap apni copy mein yeh line zaroor likhiye. (vii) aur (viii) ko ek aur tarah bhi samjha ja sakta hai: \(2\pi\) poora ek chakkar hai. Poora chakkar laga kar \(\theta\) peeche aana bilkul wahi hai jo seedha \(-\theta\) par jana. Is liye \(\cos(2\pi - \theta) = \cos(-\theta) = \cos\theta\) aur \(\sin(2\pi - \theta) = \sin(-\theta) = -\sin\theta\).
Deduction 9

Ab tan ki baari. \(\tan = \frac{\sin}{\cos}\), aur sin aur cos ke sum formulas humare paas aa chuke hain:
\[\tan(\alpha + \beta) = \frac{\sin(\alpha + \beta)}{\cos(\alpha + \beta)}\]
\[= \frac{\sin\alpha\cos\beta + \cos\alpha\sin\beta}{\cos\alpha\cos\beta - \sin\alpha\sin\beta}\]
\[= \dfrac{\dfrac{\sin\alpha\cos\beta}{\cos\alpha\cos\beta} + \dfrac{\cos\alpha\sin\beta}{\cos\alpha\cos\beta}}{\dfrac{\cos\alpha\cos\beta}{\cos\alpha\cos\beta} - \dfrac{\sin\alpha\sin\beta}{\cos\alpha\cos\beta}}\]
[Numerator aur denominator dono ko \(\cos\alpha\cos\beta\) se divide karne par]

blocks.text_alt: tan of (alpha plus beta) equals (tan alpha plus tan beta) over (1 minus tan alpha tan beta), result (ix)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
\(\cos\alpha\cos eta\) se hi divide kyun kiya? Kyun ke \( rac{\sin\alpha}{\cos\alpha} = 	an\alpha\). Divide karne ke baad har fraction cut-cut kar \(	an\alpha\), \(	an eta\), \(1\) ya \(	an\alpha	an eta\) ban jata hai, aur formula sirf tan mein aa jata hai. Shart: \(\cos\alpha 
e 0\), \(\cos eta 
e 0\) aur \(1 - 	an\alpha	an eta 
e 0\), warna zero se divide hoga, jo mumkin nahin.
Deduction 10

Bilkul isi tarah difference ke liye:
\[\tan(\alpha - \beta) = \frac{\sin(\alpha - \beta)}{\cos(\alpha - \beta)}\]
\[= \frac{\sin\alpha\cos\beta - \cos\alpha\sin\beta}{\cos\alpha\cos\beta + \sin\alpha\sin\beta}\]
\[= \dfrac{\dfrac{\sin\alpha\cos\beta}{\cos\alpha\cos\beta} - \dfrac{\cos\alpha\sin\beta}{\cos\alpha\cos\beta}}{\dfrac{\cos\alpha\cos\beta}{\cos\alpha\cos\beta} + \dfrac{\sin\alpha\sin\beta}{\cos\alpha\cos\beta}}\]
[Numerator aur denominator dono ko \(\cos\alpha\cos\beta\) se divide karne par]

blocks.text_alt: tan of (alpha minus beta) equals (tan alpha minus tan beta) over (1 plus tan alpha tan beta), result (x)

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Yeh hamari practice hai, kitab ka sawal nahin: \(\tan 75^{\circ}\) nikaaliye.
\(75^{\circ} = 45^{\circ} + 30^{\circ}\), \(\tan 45^{\circ} = 1\), \(\tan 30^{\circ} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\).
(ix) se: \(\tan 75^{\circ} = \frac{1 + \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}}{1 - \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}}\). Upar neeche \(\sqrt{3}\) se multiply karein: \(\frac{\sqrt{3} + 1}{\sqrt{3} - 1}\).
Rationalise karne ke liye upar neeche \(\sqrt{3} + 1\) se multiply: \(\frac{(\sqrt{3}+1)^{2}}{3 - 1} = \frac{4 + 2\sqrt{3}}{2} = 2 + \sqrt{3}\).
Calculator: \(\tan 75^{\circ} \approx 3.732\) aur \(2 + \sqrt{3} \approx 3.732\). Sahi!

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(\cos(\alpha - \beta) = \cos\alpha\cos\beta + \sin\alpha\sin\beta\) (asal law)
2. \(\cos(\alpha + \beta) = \cos\alpha\cos\beta - \sin\alpha\sin\beta\) (iv)
3. \(\sin(\alpha + \beta) = \sin\alpha\cos\beta + \cos\alpha\sin\beta\) (v)
4. \(\sin(\alpha - \beta) = \sin\alpha\cos\beta - \cos\alpha\sin\beta\) (vi)
5. \(\tan(\alpha \pm \beta) = \frac{\tan\alpha \pm \tan\beta}{1 \mp \tan\alpha\tan\beta}\) (ix), (x)
6. Cos mein sign ulta, sin mein sign wahi; tan mein denominator ka sign numerator ka ulta.
7. Results (i), (ii), (iii), (vii), (viii) allied angles ki pehli misaalein hain; agla topic 10.2 inhi ko phailata hai.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Signs ulat dena: \(\cos(\alpha + \beta)\) mein beech mein minus aata hai aur \(\cos(\alpha - \beta)\) mein plus. Sin mein sign bracket jaisa.
2. \(\sin(\alpha + \beta) = \sin\alpha + \sin\beta\) samajh lena. Aazmaiye: \(\alpha = \beta = 45^{\circ}\) par \(\sin 90^{\circ} = 1\), lekin \(\sin 45^{\circ} + \sin 45^{\circ} = \sqrt{2} \approx 1.41\). Ghalat!
3. Tan formula ke denominator mein sign: sum mein \(1 - \tan\alpha\tan\beta\), difference mein \(1 + \tan\alpha\tan\beta\).
4. \(\sin(-\beta)\) ko \(\sin\beta\) likh dena. Sin negative angle ka minus bahar laata hai, cos nahin.
